sources.title: TSMC tightens China AI chip curbs as new US rules close manufacturing loophole, sources say
UK borrowing beats forecasts as Healey's deficit picture improves
UK retail sales beat forecasts after government tells households to stock up
Taiwan tells Meta thousands of China-linked accounts seek to influence elections

stories.topic: TAIWAN / TSMC / CHINA / SEMICONDUCTORS / EXPORT CONTROLS
stories.headline: Sources say TSMC halts affected advanced Chinese chip orders without US licences
stories.body: Two people told Reuters that TSMC instructed affected Chinese customers’ orders at 16 nanometres and below to halt unless US export licences were obtained. Guidance generally limits those designers to older 28nm and 40nm processes without high-bandwidth memory or advanced packaging. The report links this to US rules effective 19 November that removed a prior compliance route. TSMC said it would comply with applicable regulations; Reuters could not independently verify all earlier manufacturing arrangements. This is an older 19 November catch-up discovery. No report-specific share-price or FX move was established.
stories.analysis: Licence and customer-screening requirements may constrain advanced-chip access and complicate supply chains; source-reported guidance is distinct from verified customer-by-customer outcomes.
stories.watch_next: Licences, affected orders and confirmed production or customer changes.

stories.headline: UK October borrowing is £17bn versus £18bn forecast; earlier months revised down
stories.body: ONS figures reported by Reuters put October public-sector net borrowing at £17 billion, below the £18 billion Reuters-poll median. April–September 2026/27 borrowing was revised down £3.6 billion, largely on stronger tax receipts. Cumulative April–October borrowing was £111.3 billion, still £3.3 billion above the OBR’s March forecast profile. These are separate monthly, revision and seven-month cumulative measures. Gilt futures briefly fell after the data but were broadly little changed; no precise quote clock or magnitude was established.
stories.analysis: The release offers limited fiscal relief while cumulative borrowing remains above the earlier forecast path; it does not resolve longer-term funding pressures.
stories.watch_next: Gilt auctions, later borrowing revisions and financing costs.

stories.headline: UK October retail volumes rise 0.7%, exceeding every Reuters-poll forecast
stories.body: UK retail sales volumes increased 0.7% in October from September, Reuters reported, beating every forecast in its economist poll. Annual volume growth rose to 2.3% from September’s 0.4%; that comparison is year on year, distinct from the monthly gain. The ONS cited demand for long-life supermarket groceries after government preparedness advice, alongside stronger clothing sales. No retail-release-specific sterling or gilt-yield move was verified. This is a sales-data surprise, not an inflation release, employment surprise or new BoE rate decision.
stories.analysis: Stockpiling can temporarily boost measured demand, so the release does not by itself establish a lasting acceleration in household consumption.
stories.watch_next: November spending, inflation, wages and BoE guidance.

stories.topic: TAIWAN / CHINA / META / ELECTIONS / INFORMATION SECURITY
stories.headline: Taiwan flags nearly 2,700 suspected influence accounts; Meta gives a different account
stories.body: Taiwanese officials and internal reports described nearly 2,700 accounts flagged to Meta ahead of the 28 November local elections as suspected China-linked influence activity. Officials separately cited AI-generated political videos. Meta said it removed flagged low-quality fake accounts, but said none of those accounts had posted election-related material and most had no followers. Beijing has long rejected election-interference accusations; its Taiwan Affairs Office did not respond to Reuters on this report. The allegations and platform response remain distinct. No attributable TWD or semiconductor-share reaction was established.
stories.analysis: Information-security allegations add political uncertainty without proving an immediate production disruption or independently establishing every claimed influence link.
stories.watch_next: Independent evidence, election developments and platform enforcement disclosures.
